label: FIXTURE RESULT: pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation
symptom: Customers say that transfer notifications are arriving late.

report.summary: Outbox publication stalled from about 11:09 to 11:10:20 while transfers kept committing. Delivery attempts in this window were rejected by the consumer with HTTP 401 (auth_error), which delays notifications.

findings.claim: Outbox backlog grew while transfers committed at a steady rate; oldest undelivered event aged to about 114 s.
findings.reason: Arrivals were 32 per 10 s throughout; publications dropped to 0 for about 80 s; pending peaked at 289 and the oldest age rose from 0.13 s to 114.5 s.

findings.claim: Most delivery attempts failed with HTTP 401 from the consumer: 700 of 1037, versus 337 successes.
findings.reason: The outcome counts show auth_error 700 and no network or server errors. The 401s come back at about 71 ms, the same as successes, so the consumer is responding promptly and rejecting the credentials.

findings.claim: The transfer API, DB pool and DB locks are not the bottleneck; the delay sits between the outbox and the consumer.
findings.reason: Transfers had no 500s and p99 of 0.25 s. The pool had no pending borrowers or timeouts. No DB blocking appeared in any sample.

alternatives.hypothesis: Poll or batch throughput limits (batch size 20, 1 s interval) caused the backlog rather than auth failures.
alternatives.reason: Capacity is about 20/s, well above the 3.2/s arrival rate. Publications also recovered to about 80 per 10 s, which is a catch-up burst.

alternatives.hypothesis: Slow consumer or network latency delayed deliveries.
alternatives.reason: Attempt latency is about 71 ms with no network or server errors.

limitations: The delivery log lists only the first 100 of 1037 records, so the exact start and end times of the 401 period and the cause of recovery are not directly seen.
The reason for the 401s (token expiry, rotated secret or fixture behavior) is not visible; the 1037 attempt records vs 1053 attempts reported by poll batches is an unexplained 16-attempt gap.
next_checks: Inspect how the outbox publisher obtains and refreshes its consumer credential, and compare it with what the consumer expects, around 11:08:54 to 11:10:20.
List delivery log records by time across the full window to find when 401s began and when they stopped.

report.summary: Notifications were late because the outbox stalled for ~90 s. The consumer rejected deliveries with HTTP 401, and publication resumed afterwards with a catch-up burst. The cause of the 401s is not shown.

findings.claim: Outbox publications stopped for about 90 s (≈11:08:53 to 11:10:23) while arrivals stayed steady at 32 per 10 s; pending grew to 289 and the oldest undelivered age reached 114 s.
findings.reason: Per-bucket publications were 0 for nine buckets, then 79-82 per bucket; pending and age rose monotonically during the gap.

findings.claim: The delivery stall coincides with 700 HTTP 401 auth errors from the consumer; 337 attempts succeeded and there were no 5xx or network errors.
findings.reason: Auth errors begin at 11:08:53, and consumer-side auth time (~70 ms) accounts for nearly all of the attempt latency.

findings.claim: The transfer API and the database pool were healthy, so the lateness is in outbox-to-consumer delivery only.
findings.reason: All transfers returned 201 with p99 0.25 s; the pool had no pending borrowers and no timeouts.

limitations: The tools do not show why the consumer returned 401 (credential rotation, auth mode change or consumer-side config), nor why it recovered.
The 1037 attempt records vs 1053 attempts reported by poll batches leaves 16 attempts unaccounted for.
next_checks: Check consumer and auth config history around 11:08:53 and 11:10:23 for a credential or auth-mode change; the runtime config only shows the 10:57 settings.
Check how the outbox handles 401s (retry and backoff, attempt count versus the max of 8) to confirm no messages were dropped.

alternatives.reason: Pool pending was 0 with no acquisition timeouts, and delivery logs show active attempts that returned 401 during the gap.
alternatives.hypothesis: Database blocking or pool exhaustion stalled the outbox poller.

alternatives.reason: Attempts took ~71 ms with no server or network errors, and the consumer handler ran in ~0.01 ms.
alternatives.hypothesis: Consumer slowness or timeouts caused the delay.
